issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify calculateTotalPrice(Meal) should return a double (use double precision for financial calculations), but the provided solution implements calculateTotalPrice as returning an int. This mismatch can confuse students about the correct return type and leads to inconsistent implementations/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the calculateTotalPrice method return double to match the specification. Update the signature to public static double calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal) and compute the sum using a double (e.g., double sum = 0.0; sum += ingredient.getPrice();). Ensure any callers/tests expect a double. Alternatively, if integer prices are intended, update the problem statement/UML to indicate an int return type to remove the discrepancy.
